survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This ICCS 2022 national report for Malta describes the ICCS study design (intact classrooms sampled within schools; all students in selected classrooms assessed; teachers and heads of school surveyed) and reports descriptive statistics and regression results. The report explicitly states that some percentages (e.g., participation in elections) are weighted by the size of the student school population, but it does not provide the specific student weight variable name(s) or replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife). The report also does not describe whether the regression analyses were conducted with complex survey weights or with unweighted data; therefore, weighting strategy details are incomplete. No ML algorithms are trained; the analysis is based on ICCS scale scores derived from IRT/Rasch procedures and conventional statistical tests/regression.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This report does not present a machine-learning analysis of PV-based cognitive achievement outcomes. The main reported outcome is ICCS civic knowledge scale scores derived from Rasch scaling of test items, and many other outcomes are questionnaire-based attitude/engagement scales. Because the dependent variables are not analyzed as PV-based achievement scores in an ML pipeline, PV handling is not applicable; additionally, the report does not document any missing-data strategy for the reported regression/scale analyses, representing a reporting gap for missingness handling.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: For Malta, the target population was grade 9 students (because the average age of grade 8 students was <13.5 years). All 42 secondary schools in Malta and Gozo were included; the core survey used computer-based assessment in 29 schools (2720 students) and a bridging paper-based delivery in 13 schools (1180 students). Intact classrooms were selected within sampled schools and all students in selected classrooms participated. The analytic sample described in the report is the Maltese student group comprising 3900 students (2023 males, 1877 females) from 14 State, 21 Church, and 7 Independent schools; the report does not specify additional exclusions beyond the described sampling and mode assignment.

data.outcome_summary: This ICCS 2022 national report for Malta uses the ICCS civic knowledge scale (derived from Rasch scaling of test items) and relates it to engagement-related questionnaire predictors using regression analysis. For the engagement predictor model, the report reports that the twelve engagement predictors explain 33.0% of the total variation in ICCS civic knowledge scores, with most predictors significant at p < 0.05. The strongest predictor is students’ expected participation in illegal protest activities (lowest p-value), with a negative regression coefficient (−3.425). The report also notes that two engagement aspects—participation in wider community groups/organisations and willingness to participate in school activities—were not significant. No machine-learning algorithms are trained; therefore, ML technique fields are empty and the analysis is conventional regression rather than predictive ML.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction targets an official assessment framework, user guide, or technical manual without an empirical ML study. Sample sizes, ML algorithms, and predictive findings are intentionally null or empty per schema rules for non-empirical IEA/OECD documentation.
